The ending feels deeply purposeful and earned because it provides emotional and thematic closure to the traumatic event at the center of the story. Rather than stopping abruptly right after the chaos of the shooting, the narrative moves forward in time—first to the birth of Barbara's baby and the aftermath of the tragedy, and finally to decades later. The final paragraph resolves the central mystery of Barbara's character arc: why she instinctively stood up and walked toward the gunman. By focusing on her recurring dream, the conclusion ties together the themes of human connection, private grief (echoing the rabbi's final sermon), and the loss of innocence, arriving at the exact poignant realization the entire piece was building toward.
